preconditions.description: The number of students n is between 2 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(students) == n and all(1 <= f <= n and f != i and s in (1, 2) for i, (f, s) in enumerate(students, start=1))
preconditions.description: There are exactly n student records; for each student i, their best friend f is a valid student index different from i, and sex s is 1 (boy) or 2 (girl).

postconditions.expression: len(pairs) == t and all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and a != b for a, b in pairs)
postconditions.description: The output contains exactly t pairs, each consisting of two distinct valid student indices.

postconditions.expression: len(set(p for pair in pairs for p in pair)) == 2 * t
postconditions.description: Each student appears in at most one pair (all 2*t elements in the pairs are distinct).

postconditions.expression: all((students[a-1][0] == b) and (students[b-1][0] == a) for a, b in pairs)
postconditions.description: Every pair (a, b) consists of mutual best friends: a's best friend is b and b's best friend is a.

postconditions.expression: e == sum(1 for a, b in pairs if (students[a-1][1] == 1 and students[b-1][1] == 2) or (students[a-1][1] == 2 and students[b-1][1] == 1))
postconditions.description: The value e equals the count of boy-girl pairs in the output.

postconditions.expression: t == max(len(p) for p in all_valid_pair_sets)
postconditions.description: The number of pairs t is the maximum possible number of mutual best-friend pairs that can be formed from the input.

postconditions.expression: e == max(sum(1 for a, b in p if (students[a-1][1] == 1 and students[b-1][1] == 2) or (students[a-1][1] == 2 and students[b-1][1] == 1)) for p in all_valid_pair_sets if len(p) == t)
postconditions.description: Among all sets of pairs with the maximum size t, the value e is the maximum possible number of boy-girl pairs.
